description: One Rudder Cloud home: what holds its memory, how stalled it is, what its agents are doing, and whether its terminals stay connected.

panels.description: Memory the kernel can hand out without swapping. Below 12% the cleanup runs early; red means the home is close to the OOM state of 2026-11-02. Check Memory by process group below.
panels.title: Memory available

panels.description: Share of swap in use. No swap means the machine booted from an image without the swap file; the scaler recommends add-swap. Red means swap is nearly full and the next spike will stall the machine.
panels.title: Swap used

panels.description: Share of the last 10 seconds every task waited for memory (PSI full avg10). Red means the machine is thrashing right now: terminals lag, then drop.
panels.title: Memory stall

panels.description: Free space on /workspace, where checkouts, builds and caches live. Red means builds will start failing: extend the volume.
panels.title: Disk free

panels.description: Agents in a live turn on this home.
panels.title: Agents working

panels.description: Agents with a live process and no turn. They hold memory until the cleanup puts them to sleep.
panels.title: Agents idle

panels.description: Agents the cleanup parked. One message wakes them.
panels.title: Agents asleep

panels.description: Whether the supervisor's control socket to the control plane is open, as the home sees it. Disconnected means attached terminals show "Cloud machine reconnecting"; check memory stall and the supervisor event loop.
panels.title: Control socket

panels.description: Resident memory summed per process group, stacked, with memory in use (total minus available) and the machine's total as lines. Claude growing with many idle agents is what the cleanup fixes; used close to total with no swap is the 2026-11-02 failure.
panels.title: Memory by process group

panels.description: Swap in use against the swap size (dashed). A flat zero total means the home has no swap and nothing cushions a memory spike.
panels.title: Swap

panels.description: Share of the last 10 seconds tasks waited for memory: full means every task, some means at least one. The cleanup runs early once full (over a minute) reaches the red line; staying above it means the home needs more memory.
panels.title: Memory stall

panels.description: Share of the last 10 seconds tasks waited for disk. High IO stall together with memory stall usually means the kernel is evicting and rereading files because memory is short.
panels.title: IO stall

panels.description: Share of the last 10 seconds tasks waited for a CPU. High CPU stall with low memory stall means too many builds or agents are running at once for 4 CPUs.
panels.title: CPU stall

panels.description: Live agents on this home. Idle agents hold memory for nothing; the hourly cleanup moves the untouched ones to asleep.
panels.title: Agents by state

panels.description: One minute load average against the CPU count (dashed). Load far above the CPU count with high memory stall means tasks are blocked on memory, not computing (the 2026-11-02 home sat at 235 on 4 CPUs).
panels.title: Load and CPUs

panels.description: Free space as a share of each disk. Below the red line on /workspace builds start failing: extend the volume. The root disk filling usually means logs or temp files outside /workspace.
panels.title: Disk free by mount

panels.description: Processes on the machine. A steady climb with flat agent counts means something is leaking processes (watchers, dev servers); the cleanup stops leftovers older than an hour.
panels.title: Processes

panels.description: How late the supervisor's event loop runs. It relays every terminal, so above the amber line typing lags and above the red line sockets time out. Usually caused by memory stall on the machine.
panels.title: Supervisor event loop delay

panels.description: The control socket over time, as the home sees it and as the control plane sees it. Red stretches are when attached terminals showed "Cloud machine reconnecting". If only the control plane shows red, the home thinks it is connected while the control plane does not.
panels.title: Control socket

panels.description: Times the supervisor reopened its control socket, in 5 minute buckets. Each one dropped every attached terminal briefly. Repeated reconnects follow memory stall or a slow event loop.
panels.title: Control reconnects, per 5 minutes

panels.description: Cleanup runs in hourly buckets. Hourly is the schedule, memory means the home ran short and the cleanup ran early, boot is the first run after a start. Memory runs every hour mean the cleanup cannot free enough: the home needs more memory.
panels.title: Cleanup runs per hour by trigger

panels.description: Cleanup runs per hour that did not finish. Any bar here means idle agents were not put to sleep that hour: check the cleanup log on the home (~/.rudder/cleanup).
panels.title: Cleanup runs that failed or timed out

panels.description: What the cleanup did: park puts an idle agent to sleep, stop ends a leftover process (a dev server, watcher or test runner an agent forgot).
panels.title: Cleanup actions per hour

panels.description: Seconds since the control plane last heard this home's heartbeat (sent every 30 seconds while the home is running). Past the red line the control plane treats the home as gone; if the home's own metrics still arrive, its supervisor is stuck.
panels.title: Heartbeat age

panels.description: Terminals, phones and browsers attached to this home through the control plane. These are the people who see "reconnecting" when the control socket drops.
panels.title: Attached clients

panels.description: Control socket closes for this home as the control plane counted them. Compare with Control reconnects above: closes the home never noticed point at the network or the control plane.
panels.title: Disconnects, per 5 minutes

title: Rudder home machine
